ai.description: This slender skink reaches 15 cm. It is brown with white spots along the flanks and a pale underside. It features a wedge-shaped snout and reduced, pentadactyl limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Riopa albopunctata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, small white spot on each scale of the dorsum, which creates a unique, uniform speckled pattern.
ai.habitat: The White-spotted Supple Skink inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The White-spotted Supple Skink is primarily crepuscular, emerging during twilight hours to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Riopa albopunctata* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Riopa albopunctata* is found in the Indian subcontinent across the Gangetic plains and central India, typically inhabiting low-elevation forests and scrublands.
